target: O que você quer de presente?
english: What do you want as a gift?
grammar: Portuguese questions often have the same word order as statements — just change the intonation.

target: O cheiro da comida está ótimo.
english: The smell of the food is great.

target: Essa rua é muito perigosa à noite.
english: This street is very dangerous at night.
grammar: 'Ser' describes inherent or permanent qualities — characteristics that define someone or something.

target: Por que ele está de mau humor?
english: Why is he in a bad mood?
grammar: 'Por que' (why?) is two words. 'Porque' (because) is one word. 'Por quê?' at sentence end.

target: Os filhos deles estudam na mesma escola.
english: Their children study at the same school.
grammar: 'Deles' = theirs/of them (de + eles, masculine). 'Delas' = de + elas (feminine). Used to clarify 'seu/sua' which can be ambiguous.

target: O mapa da cidade está no celular.
english: The city map is on the phone.
grammar: 'Mapa' is masculine despite ending in -a: o mapa. Other exceptions: o dia, o cinema, o problema, o tema, o sistema.

target: Eu fui à festa da empresa ontem.
english: I went to the company party yesterday.

target: Uma xícara de chá me faz bem.
english: A cup of tea does me good.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: O nome do restaurante é difícil de lembrar.
english: The restaurant's name is hard to remember.
grammar: 'O nome' is masculine despite ending in -e. Some -e words are masculine: nome, leite, café.

target: A estação do metrô fica a dois quarteirões.
english: The subway station is two blocks away.
grammar: 'Ficar' for permanent locations: 'o hotel fica perto' = the hotel is (located) near. More specific than 'estar.'

target: A festa na casa da Ana foi ótima.
english: The party at Ana's house was great.

target: A água do rio é clara e fria.
english: The river water is clear and cold.
grammar: 'De + o/a/os/as' always contracts to 'do/da/dos/das' — these contractions are mandatory, never optional.

target: O horário do almoço é das doze às duas.
english: Lunch time is from twelve to two.

target: Vou à padaria comprar pão.
english: I'm going to the bakery to buy bread.

target: Eu fui ao mercado comprar frutas.
english: I went to the market to buy fruit.
grammar: Definite articles agree in gender and number: o/a/os/as. Portuguese uses articles more than English.

target: Estou com preguiça de ir à academia.
english: I'm feeling lazy about going to the gym.
grammar: Portuguese uses 'estar com' + noun where English uses 'to be' + adjective: 'estou com fome' (I'm hungry), 'estou com frio' (I'm cold).

target: Como é que eu faço para reservar?
english: How do I go about making a reservation?
grammar: 'Como é que' is a very common Brazilian reinforcement of 'como.' Adding 'é que' makes questions sound more natural and conversational.

target: O quadro na parede é do meu avô.
english: The painting on the wall is my grandfather's.

target: Os livros da estante são do meu irmão.
english: The books on the shelf are my brother's.
grammar: Definite articles agree in gender and number: o/a/os/as. Portuguese uses articles more than English.

target: Ele é do Rio, mas mora em São Paulo.
english: He's from Rio, but lives in São Paulo.
grammar: Origin uses 'ser' (é do Rio = permanent) while current residence can use 'morar' (mora em SP = where he currently lives).

target: O restaurante é mais caro do que eu pensava.
english: The restaurant is more expensive than I thought.
grammar: Comparatives use 'mais + adjective + do que': mais caro do que = more expensive than. The 'do' is optional in speech.

target: Ele é tímido no começo, mas depois se abre.
english: He's shy at first, but opens up later.
grammar: 'Em + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'no/na/nos/nas' — always use the contracted form.

target: O Brasil é o maior país da América do Sul.
english: Brazil is the largest country in South America.
grammar: 'Ser' is used with comparisons and superlatives to describe inherent qualities.

target: Vou ao banco pagar as contas.
english: I'm going to the bank to pay the bills.
grammar: 'Ao' is the contraction of 'a + o' (to the, masculine). 'Vou ao banco' = I go to the bank.

target: Minha mãe é baiana, nasceu em Salvador.
english: My mom is Bahian, she was born in Salvador.
grammar: Origin and birthplace are permanent — always use 'ser.' 'É baiana' = she is Bahian (forever).

target: Esse restaurante é tão bom quanto caro.
english: This restaurant is as good as it is expensive.
grammar: Contractions with 'aqui/ali/aquilo': de+aqui=daqui (from here), de+ali=dali (from there) — common in everyday speech.

target: O apartamento novo é maior que o antigo.
english: The new apartment is bigger than the old one.
grammar: 'Maior' means bigger/larger. It's an irregular comparative — you don't say 'mais grande.' Similarly: menor (smaller), melhor (better), pior (worse).

target: O que aconteceu?
english: What happened?
grammar: 'O que' = what. 'Acontecer' means 'to happen.' Past tense here: 'aconteceu' (pretérito perfeito).

target: Quem inventou isso?
english: Who invented this?

target: Onde é a saída?
english: Where's the exit?
grammar: 'Onde é' = where is (permanent location). Use 'onde é' for places, 'onde está' for movable things.

target: Quem é o gerente?
english: Who's the manager?

target: Qual é o problema?
english: What's the problem?

target: Quem é aquele cara?
english: Who's that guy?
grammar: 'Cara' is informal Brazilian Portuguese for 'guy/dude.' Very common in everyday speech.

target: Como está o trânsito?
english: How's the traffic?
grammar: Portuguese questions often have the same word order as statements — just change the intonation.

target: Qual é o seu nome?
english: What's your name?
grammar: 'Qual' means 'which/what' when choosing from options or asking for specific information. 'Qual é o seu nome?' is the standard way to ask someone's name.

target: Qual é a sua profissão?
english: What's your profession?

target: Quando você chega?
english: When do you arrive?
grammar: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions often keep statement word order: 'Quando você chega?' not 'Quando chega você?'

target: Onde você mora?
english: Where do you live?
grammar: 'Onde' = where. 'Morar' means 'to live/reside.' 'Onde você mora?' is one of the most common questions.

target: Quando eles chegam?
english: When do they arrive?

target: Onde você trabalha?
english: Where do you work?

target: Onde posso estacionar?
english: Where can I park?

target: Onde eu assino?
english: Where do I sign?
grammar: 'Onde' = where. 'Aonde' = where to (with motion verbs): 'aonde você vai?'

target: Falou, até depois!
english: Alright, see you later!
grammar: 'Falou' (literally 'spoke') is a casual goodbye in Brazil, like 'later' or 'peace out.' Often combined: 'falou, valeu!'

target: Quem é aquela pessoa?
english: Who is that person?
grammar: 'Quem' = who. 'Aquela' is the feminine demonstrative for 'that (over there).' 'Aquele' for masculine.

target: Quem fez esse bolo?
english: Who made this cake?
grammar: 'Quem' as subject: 'Quem fez?' = Who made? The verb agrees with the implied subject (third person singular).

target: Quando vocês se mudaram?
english: When did you move?
grammar: 'Quando vocês se mudaram?' — 'mudar-se' is reflexive: to move (house). 'Mudar' alone = to change.

target: Quem trouxe o bolo?
english: Who brought the cake?

target: Como foi a viagem?
english: How was the trip?

target: O que você recomenda?
english: What do you recommend?
grammar: Portuguese questions often have the same word order as statements — just change the intonation.

target: Por que vocês estão rindo?
english: Why are you laughing?
grammar: 'Por que' (two words) is used in questions. 'Porque' (one word) is for answers. This is one of the trickiest spelling rules in Portuguese.

target: Quando é o seu aniversário?
english: When is your birthday?
grammar: 'Quando é' = when is. 'Aniversário' is used for both birthday and anniversary in Portuguese.

target: Por que você está triste?
english: Why are you sad?
grammar: 'Por que' + estar for temporary states: 'Por que você está triste?' uses 'estar' because moods are temporary.

target: Quem é o responsável aqui?
english: Who's in charge here?
grammar: 'Quem é o responsável' = who is in charge. Useful in work and service situations.

target: Como é o seu apartamento?
english: What's your apartment like?
grammar: 'Como é' literally means 'how is' but translates to 'what is it like' — used to ask for descriptions.

target: Onde tem um caixa eletrônico?
english: Where's there an ATM?

target: Como foi o seu dia?
english: How was your day?

target: Onde a gente pode sentar?
english: Where can we sit?

target: O que você está lendo?
english: What are you reading?

target: Quando a gente pode conversar?
english: When can we talk?

target: Quando é o próximo feriado?
english: When's the next holiday?

target: O que tem na geladeira?
english: What's in the fridge?

target: Qual caminho é mais rápido?
english: Which way is faster?

target: Como é que isso funciona?
english: How does this work?

target: Quem está tocando a campainha?
english: Who's ringing the doorbell?
grammar: 'Quem' = who. Invariable — no plural form: 'quem são essas pessoas?'

target: As contas do mês chegaram.
english: The monthly bills arrived.

target: O endereço da empresa mudou.
english: The company address changed.

target: Qual é a senha do Wi-Fi?
english: What's the Wi-Fi password?
grammar: 'Qual é a senha' = what's the password. 'Senha' means password, PIN, or queue number in Brazil.

target: O que tem dentro da mochila?
english: What's inside the backpack?

target: Qual é o código do portão?
english: What's the gate code?

target: Qual é a sua cor favorita?
english: What's your favorite color?
grammar: 'Qual' = which/what. 'Qual é o seu nome?' is more common than 'Como é o seu nome?'

target: A calçada da rua está quebrada.
english: The sidewalk is broken.
grammar: 'da' contracts de+a — mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Quando você volta?
english: When are you coming back?
grammar: 'Quando você volta?' — 'Voltar' = to come back/return. Present tense used for near future plans.

target: Quando a reunião começa?
english: When does the meeting start?
grammar: 'Quando' + present tense for scheduled events: 'Quando a reunião começa?' = When does the meeting start?

target: Quando termina o expediente?
english: When does the workday end?

target: Quem mora nesse apartamento?
english: Who lives in that apartment?

target: Quando vocês vão casar?
english: When are you getting married?

target: Quando começa o show?
english: When does the show start?

target: Onde você aprendeu português?
english: Where did you learn Portuguese?

target: Por favor, pode repetir?
english: Please, can you repeat that?
grammar: The perfeito of 'ser' and 'ir' are identical: 'fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram' — context makes the meaning clear.

target: Como você veio para cá?
english: How did you get here?
grammar: 'Como' asking about manner/method: 'Como você veio?' = How did you come? Expects a method answer.

target: Onde a gente se encontra?
english: Where do we meet up?
grammar: 'Onde a gente se encontra?' — reflexive 'se encontrar' = to meet up. 'A gente' = we (informal).

target: Por que o voo atrasou?
english: Why was the flight delayed?
grammar: 'Por que' for asking reasons about events: 'Por que o voo atrasou?' = Why was the flight delayed?

target: O que significa essa palavra?
english: What does this word mean?
grammar: 'O que significa' = what does it mean. Very useful for language learners! 'Essa' = this (feminine).

target: O que está escrito ali?
english: What does it say there?

target: Eu gosto do clima daqui.
english: I like the weather here.
grammar: 'Daqui' = de + aqui (from here). Similar contractions: dali (de + ali), daí (de + aí), daquele (de + aquele).

target: O dia está lindo hoje.
english: The day is beautiful today.
grammar: 'Dia' is masculine (o dia) despite ending in -a. It's one of the most common exceptions to the gender rule.

target: Como é a vida no Brasil?
english: What's life like in Brazil?

target: Por que o elevador não funciona?
english: Why isn't the elevator working?

target: Por que não tem Wi-Fi aqui?
english: Why isn't there Wi-Fi here?
grammar: 'Por que' (why?) is two words. 'Porque' (because) is one word. 'Por quê?' at sentence end.

target: Quando a gente pode se mudar?
english: When can we move in?
grammar: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions don't require inverted punctuation like Spanish's ¿?

target: Onde tem sinal de celular aqui?
english: Where's there cell service here?
grammar: 'Onde' = where. 'Aonde' = where to (with motion verbs): 'aonde você vai?'

target: A sala de espera está lotada.
english: The waiting room is packed.
grammar: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

target: Uma fatia de pizza, por favor.
english: A slice of pizza, please.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: A porta do banheiro está trancada.
english: The bathroom door is locked.

target: Um litro de leite, por favor.
english: A liter of milk, please.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: O barulho da rua me incomoda.
english: The street noise bothers me.
grammar: 'da' contracts de+a — mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: A qualidade dos produtos é boa.
english: The product quality is good.
grammar: 'dos' contracts de+os — mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Ele precisa de um computador novo.
english: He needs a new computer.

target: Qual é a sua opinião sobre isso?
english: What's your opinion on this?
grammar: 'Qual' = which/what. 'Qual é o seu nome?' is more common than 'Como é o seu nome?'

target: Eu gosto de cozinhar para os amigos.
english: I like cooking for friends.
grammar: 'Gostar de' + infinitive: 'gosto de cozinhar.' 'Para os amigos' = for friends. Purpose with 'para.'

target: Os vizinhos do andar de cima são barulhentos.
english: The upstairs neighbors are noisy.
grammar: 'vizinhos' — diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: O trânsito na hora do rush é terrível.
english: Rush hour traffic is terrible.

target: Qual sorvete você prefere?
english: Which ice cream do you prefer?

target: Como ficou o bolo?
english: How did the cake turn out?
grammar: 'Ficar' is used to describe how something turned out or ended up. 'Como ficou?' = How did it come out?

target: Quando sai o resultado?
english: When does the result come out?
grammar: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions don't require inverted punctuation like Spanish's ¿?

target: Bom dia! Dormiu bem?
english: Good morning! Did you sleep well?
grammar: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Como funciona o metrô daqui?
english: How does the subway work here?
grammar: 'Como' = how. 'Funcionar' = to work/function. 'Daqui' = de + aqui = from here/around here.

target: O que você vai querer?
english: What are you going to have?
grammar: 'O que' for 'what' in questions about things. 'Vai querer' = will want — near future with 'ir + infinitive.'

target: Quem vai levar as crianças?
english: Who's going to take the kids?
grammar: 'Quem vai' = who will. 'Levar' = to take (someone somewhere). 'Buscar' = to pick up (the opposite).

target: Quando posso marcar a consulta?
english: When can I schedule the appointment?

target: Quando a obra vai terminar?
english: When will the construction be finished?
grammar: 'Quando' = when. Portuguese questions don't require inverted punctuation like Spanish's ¿?

target: Por que tem tanta fila?
english: Why is the line so long?
grammar: 'Por que' (why?) is two words. 'Porque' (because) is one word. 'Por quê?' at sentence end.

target: O livro está na estante.
english: The book is on the shelf.
grammar: 'O' is the masculine definite article. Most nouns ending in -o are masculine: o livro, o carro, o gato.

target: Eu moro num bairro tranquilo.
english: I live in a quiet neighborhood.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: Os documentos estão na pasta.
english: The documents are in the folder.

target: Quem é o dono desse carro?
english: Who's the owner of this car?

target: Como você conheceu a sua esposa?
english: How did you meet your wife?

target: Qual é o prato do dia?
english: What's the dish of the day?

target: Por que você escolheu essa carreira?
english: Why did you choose this career?
grammar: 'Por que' (why?) is two words. 'Porque' (because) is one word. 'Por quê?' at sentence end.

target: Quando você começou a trabalhar aqui?
english: When did you start working here?

target: Onde vocês vão passar as férias?
english: Where are you spending your vacation?

target: Por que não me avisaram antes?
english: Why didn't they tell me before?

target: Eu moro no centro da cidade.
english: I live in the city center.
grammar: 'No' is the contraction of 'em + o' (in the, masculine). 'Na' is 'em + a' (in the, feminine). Both are mandatory.

target: O pai dele trabalha no hospital.
english: His dad works at the hospital.
grammar: 'O pai' = the father. Family terms change gender: pai/mãe, filho/filha, irmão/irmã.

target: A noite está agradável para caminhar.
english: The evening is pleasant for walking.
grammar: 'Noite' is feminine: a noite. Time periods: a manhã (morning), a tarde (afternoon), a noite (night). All feminine.

target: O resultado do exame sai amanhã.
english: The exam result comes out tomorrow.

target: Qual é a melhor praia por aqui?
english: What's the best beach around here?

target: Por que a internet está tão lenta?
english: Why is the internet so slow?

target: A casa dela fica perto do parque.
english: Her house is near the park.
grammar: 'A' is the feminine definite article. Most nouns ending in -a are feminine: a casa, a mesa, a porta.

target: O ônibus dos alunos chega às sete.
english: The students' bus arrives at seven.
grammar: 'Dos' is the contraction of 'de + os' (of the, masculine plural). 'Das' = 'de + as' (feminine plural).

target: Ele comprou um apartamento perto do trabalho.
english: He bought an apartment near work.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: Os gatos da vizinha são muito barulhentos.
english: The neighbor's cats are very noisy.

target: A reunião da equipe é toda segunda.
english: The team meeting is every Monday.

target: A piscina do condomínio fecha às dez.
english: The condo pool closes at ten.
grammar: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

target: O porteiro do prédio é muito prestativo.
english: The building doorman is very helpful.
grammar: 'Porteiro' is a very common figure in Brazilian apartments — the doorman/concierge who manages building access.

target: Eu preciso de ajuda com essa mudança.
english: I need help with this move.
grammar: 'Precisar de' means 'to need.' The 'de' is required: 'preciso de ajuda,' not 'preciso ajuda.' However, before infinitives, many Brazilians drop the 'de.'

target: A escola das crianças é perto de casa.
english: The kids' school is near home.

target: A comida da minha mãe é a melhor.
english: My mom's cooking is the best.

target: Vamos aos correios amanhã.
english: Let's go to the post office tomorrow.
grammar: 'Aos' is the contraction of 'a + os' (to the, masculine plural). 'Às' = 'a + as' (feminine plural).

target: Quem vai estar na reunião?
english: Who's going to be at the meeting?

target: A televisão está na sala.
english: The TV is in the living room.
grammar: Nouns ending in -ão are usually masculine: o avião, o coração, o limão. But some are feminine: a mão, a televisão, a estação.

target: O que você faz da vida?
english: What do you do for a living?
grammar: 'O que' means 'what.' 'Fazer da vida' is the natural way to ask about someone's profession in Brazil.

target: Como se diz isso em português?
english: How do you say this in Portuguese?
grammar: 'Como' means 'how.' 'Como se diz' is the impersonal way to ask — literally 'how does one say.'

target: Por que não vamos à praia?
english: Why don't we go to the beach?
grammar: 'Por que não' = why don't we. 'Vamos à praia' — 'à' is the contraction of 'a + a' (to the, feminine).

target: O que você acha dessa ideia?
english: What do you think of this idea?
grammar: 'O que você acha de' is the go-to phrase for asking opinions in Brazilian Portuguese. Much more common than 'o que você pensa.'

target: Quem vai ficar com as crianças?
english: Who's going to stay with the kids?

target: Como se escreve o seu sobrenome?
english: How do you spell your last name?
grammar: 'Como se escreve' = how does one write/spell. Very useful when filling out forms or making reservations.

target: As praias do Nordeste são maravilhosas.
english: The beaches of the Northeast are wonderful.
grammar: 'As praias' — feminine plural. 'Do Nordeste' = de + o = of the Northeast. 'Nordeste' is masculine.

target: Eu peguei o livro na biblioteca.
english: I got the book from the library.

target: Uma colher de açúcar no café.
english: A spoonful of sugar in the coffee.
grammar: Indefinite articles: 'um' (masculine), 'uma' (feminine). 'Uns/umas' for plural 'some.'

target: Eu deixei a carteira no carro.
english: I left my wallet in the car.

target: A entrada do cinema é por aqui.
english: The movie theater entrance is this way.
grammar: 'Por' indicates cause, means, or exchange — contrast with 'para' which signals purpose or destination.

target: O ponto de ônibus fica na esquina.
english: The bus stop is at the corner.

target: As toalhas estão no armário do banheiro.
english: The towels are in the bathroom cabinet.

target: Os moradores do prédio reclamaram do barulho.
english: The building residents complained about the noise.

target: Eu fui à praia com os amigos.
english: I went to the beach with friends.

target: O que você fez no fim de semana?
english: What did you do on the weekend?

target: O que a gente leva para a festa?
english: What do we bring to the party?

target: Eu comprei uma passagem de avião para Salvador.
english: I bought a plane ticket to Salvador.

target: A gente gosta de dormir com a janela aberta.
english: We like sleeping with the window open.

target: Quem vai cuidar do cachorro?
english: Who's going to take care of the dog?
grammar: 'Quem' = who. Invariable — no plural form: 'quem são essas pessoas?'

target: Quando ele vai entregar o relatório?
english: When is he going to deliver the report?

target: Uma amiga minha trabalha nesse banco.
english: A friend of mine works at this bank.
grammar: 'Nesse' is the contraction of 'em + esse' (in this). Other contractions: neste (em + este), naquele (em + aquele), nisso (em + isso).

target: Ele vai ao shopping comprar roupa.
english: He's going to the mall to buy clothes.

target: Eu vi um filme ótimo no cinema.
english: I saw a great movie at the theater.

target: Ela tem uma amiga que mora no Japão.
english: She has a friend who lives in Japan.
grammar: 'Uma amiga' — indefinite feminine article. 'Amigo' (masc.) / 'Amiga' (fem.) — the ending changes with gender.

target: A ponte sobre o rio é muito antiga.
english: The bridge over the river is very old.

target: O filme foi tão bom quanto o livro.
english: The movie was as good as the book.
grammar: 'Tão + adjective + quanto' means 'as... as': 'tão bom quanto' = as good as. You can also use 'como' instead of 'quanto.'

target: Quando vamos nos ver de novo?
english: When are we going to see each other again?

target: O que vocês vão fazer no feriado?
english: What are you going to do on the holiday?

target: Eu preciso ir ao dentista essa semana.
english: I need to go to the dentist this week.

target: Ela mora numa casa com um jardim grande.
english: She lives in a house with a big garden.
grammar: 'Numa' is the contraction of 'em + uma' (in a, feminine). 'Num' = 'em + um' (masculine). Very common in speech.

target: A padaria da esquina tem o melhor pão.
english: The bakery on the corner has the best bread.

target: Estou procurando a estação de trem, pode me ajudar?
english: I'm looking for the train station, can you help me?
grammar: Regular -ar verbs in the preterite: the eu form ends in -ei, the ele/ela form ends in -ou.

target: Preciso ir ao correio mandar uma encomenda.
english: I need to go to the post office to send a package.

target: As notas dos alunos melhoraram.
english: The students' grades improved.
grammar: 'dos' contracts de+os — mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: O sistema do computador travou.
english: The computer system froze.
grammar: 'Sistema' is masculine (o sistema) despite ending in -a. Words of Greek origin ending in -ma are usually masculine: o tema, o cinema, o diploma.

target: Vocês precisam de alguma coisa?
english: Do you need anything?

target: Eu prefiro água com gás.
english: I prefer sparkling water.

target: Eu preciso de um favor.
english: I need a favor.

target: Eu preciso de mais informações.

target: A gente precisa de mais espaço.
english: We need more space.

target: Ela prefere o café mais forte.
english: She prefers stronger coffee.

target: Vocês gostam de comida picante?
english: Do you like spicy food?

target: Ele prefere café sem açúcar.
english: He prefers coffee without sugar.

target: Ela precisa de férias urgente.
english: She urgently needs a vacation.

target: Ela precisa de uma folga.
english: She needs a day off.

target: O tempo está horrível hoje.
english: The weather is terrible today.
grammar: 'Horrível' = horrible/awful. Adjectives ending in -vel are the same for masculine and feminine.

target: Eu trabalhei até tarde ontem.
english: I worked until late yesterday.
grammar: Regular -ar past: trabalhar → trabalhei (eu). First person: drop -ar, add -ei.

target: As flores do jardim estão lindas.
english: The garden flowers are beautiful.
grammar: 'As flores' — feminine plural article 'as.' Most nouns ending in -a are feminine: flor is an exception (ends in -r but is feminine).

target: O problema do trânsito é sério.
english: The traffic problem is serious.
grammar: 'Do' is the contraction of 'de + o' (of the, masculine). These contractions are mandatory — you can never say 'de o.'

target: As ruas do centro estão cheias.
english: The downtown streets are crowded.
grammar: 'estão' (estar) — marks a temporary condition, emotion, or location. Ser would imply permanence.

target: As luzes da rua estão acesas.
english: The street lights are on.
grammar: 'estão' (estar) — marks a temporary condition, emotion, or location. Ser would imply permanence.

target: O elevador do prédio é lento.
english: The building elevator is slow.

target: As escadas do prédio são íngremes.
english: The building stairs are steep.
grammar: 'é' (ser) — for permanent qualities, identity, origin. Using estar would imply a temporary state.

target: A voz dela é muito bonita.
english: Her voice is very beautiful.
grammar: 'Dele/dela' = his/her. More specific than 'seu/sua' which can mean his/her/your.

target: A fila do banco está enorme.
english: The bank line is huge.
grammar: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

target: A vista do apartamento é incrível.
english: The apartment view is incredible.

target: A greve dos motoristas atrapalhou tudo.
english: The drivers' strike disrupted everything.
grammar: 'dos' contracts de+os — mandatory in Portuguese, these preposition+article fusions are never written separately.

target: Eu preciso de silêncio para estudar.
english: I need silence to study.

target: Nós precisamos de paciência para esperar.
english: We need patience to wait.

target: Eu prefiro o horário da manhã.
english: I prefer the morning schedule.

target: Nós saímos cedo do trabalho ontem.
english: We left work early yesterday.
grammar: Regular -ir verbs in the past: -i, -iu, -imos, -iram. 'Sair' → 'saí' (eu), 'saiu' (ele/ela).

target: Eu paguei a conta do restaurante.
english: I paid the restaurant bill.
grammar: Regular -ar past: pagar → paguei. Spelling change: g → gu before -ei (like ligar → liguei).

target: A mochila da minha filha é rosa.
english: My daughter's backpack is pink.
grammar: 'A mochila' — feminine. Most nouns ending in -a are feminine. 'Da' = de + a (of the).

target: A foto do perfil dela é bonita.
english: Her profile picture is pretty.
grammar: 'Foto' is feminine (a foto) because it's short for 'fotografia.' Similarly, 'moto' is feminine (a moto) from 'motocicleta.'

target: Eu comparei os preços antes de comprar.
english: I compared prices before buying.
grammar: In narration, preterite carries the plot forward while imperfect provides the backdrop — mastering this distinction is essential.

target: Tem um gato no telhado.
english: There's a cat on the roof.
grammar: In Brazilian Portuguese, 'tem' is commonly used to mean 'there is/there are,' even though formal grammar prefers 'há.'

target: Eu gosto das pessoas daqui.
english: I like the people from here.

target: Eu prefiro pagar com Pix.
english: I prefer to pay with Pix.

target: Vocês preferem carne ou peixe?
english: Do you prefer meat or fish?

target: Eu comprei um presente para ela.
english: I bought a gift for her.
grammar: 'Um' is the masculine indefinite article (a/an). 'Uma' is the feminine: um livro, uma mesa.

target: Os sapatos estão debaixo da cama.
english: The shoes are under the bed.
grammar: 'Os sapatos' — masculine plural. 'Debaixo da cama' = under the bed. 'Da' = de + a.

target: Ela não gosta de acordar cedo.
english: She doesn't like waking up early.
grammar: 'Gostar de' + infinitive for activities: 'não gosta de acordar.' The 'de' is always required before the verb.

target: Nós preferimos ficar em casa hoje.
english: We prefer to stay home today.

target: Ela prefere morar perto do trabalho.
english: She prefers to live near work.

target: Eu prefiro não falar sobre isso.
english: I'd rather not talk about that.

target: O café está quente e forte.
english: The coffee is hot and strong.
grammar: Adjectives ending in -e don't change for gender: quente is the same for masculine and feminine. Only number changes: quentes.

target: O quarto é pequeno, mas aconchegante.
english: The room is small but cozy.
grammar: 'Aconchegante' means cozy/warm/inviting. It's an adjective ending in -e, so it doesn't change for gender: o quarto aconchegante, a casa aconchegante.

target: O suco está gelado e refrescante.
english: The juice is ice-cold and refreshing.
grammar: Key contractions: de+o=do, de+a=da, em+o=no, em+a=na, a+o=ao, a+a=à — you must use these, never write 'de o' separately.

target: Eu falei com o gerente ontem.
english: I spoke with the manager yesterday.
grammar: The pretérito perfeito describes a completed past action — here, a single event that happened and ended.

target: Eu emprestei dinheiro para um amigo.
english: I lent money to a friend.
grammar: 'Emprestar' in Brazilian Portuguese means both 'to lend' and 'to borrow.' Context clarifies: 'emprestei PARA ele' = I lent to him. 'Emprestei DELE' = I borrowed from him.

target: Ele confirmou a reserva por telefone.
english: He confirmed the reservation by phone.
grammar: Preterite vs. imperfect is the most important distinction in Portuguese past tense — completed action vs. ongoing state.

target: O filho da vizinha é muito educado.
english: The neighbor's son is very polite.

target: O dono do apartamento é muito simpático.
english: The apartment owner is very nice.
grammar: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

target: As férias dos funcionários são em janeiro.
english: The employees' vacations are in January.
grammar: 'Férias' is always plural in Portuguese — there's no singular form. 'As férias' = vacation(s).

target: O sabor do sorvete é de manga.
english: The ice cream flavor is mango.

target: A praça do bairro é muito bonita.
english: The neighborhood square is very pretty.

target: A prova da faculdade é na terça.
english: The college exam is on Tuesday.

target: Eu preciso de mais tempo para terminar.
english: I need more time to finish.
grammar: 'Precisar de' = to need (something). Like 'gostar de,' the preposition 'de' is mandatory: 'preciso de mais tempo.'

target: Eu preciso de um carro para trabalhar.
english: I need a car for work.

target: Ela escolheu o restaurante para o jantar.
english: She chose the restaurant for dinner.
grammar: Verbs ending in -car, -gar, -çar have spelling changes in 1st person preterite: fiquei, paguei, comecei — to preserve pronunciation.

target: A cor da parede combina com os móveis.
english: The wall color matches the furniture.
grammar: 'Cor' is feminine: a cor. Some nouns don't follow the -o/-a pattern and must be memorized.

target: A gente precisa de uma resposta até sexta.
english: We need an answer by Friday.

target: A gente gosta de passar o Natal em família.

target: Ela é a pessoa mais gentil que eu conheço.
english: She's the kindest person I know.

target: Nós jantamos num restaurante italiano.

target: Os meninos estão brincando no quintal.
english: The boys are playing in the backyard.

target: Ela vai à academia todo dia.
english: She goes to the gym every day.
grammar: 'À' is the contraction of 'a + a' (to the, feminine). This is the famous 'crase' — it gets its own accent mark in Portuguese.

target: A árvore do quintal está enorme.
english: The tree in the backyard is huge.
grammar: Portuguese articles contract with prepositions: de+o=do, em+a=na, a+a=à. These are never optional.

english: Social media takes a lot of time.

target: Eu coloquei os copos na pia.
english: I put the glasses in the sink.

target: As flores da praça são coloridas.
english: The flowers in the square are colorful.

target: O atendimento nesse hotel é excelente.
english: The service at this hotel is excellent.
grammar: 'Em' contracts with demonstratives: em + esse = nesse, em + aquele = naquele — always use the fused form.

target: A chave da porta está na gaveta.
english: The door key is in the drawer.
grammar: 'Da' is the contraction of 'de + a' (of the, feminine). 'Da porta' = of the door.

target: As chaves do carro estão na bolsa.
english: The car keys are in the bag.

target: O problema é a falta de tempo.
english: The problem is the lack of time.
grammar: 'Problema' is masculine (o problema) despite ending in -a. This is one of the most common gender mistakes learners make.

target: A temperatura do ar-condicionado está muito baixa.
english: The air conditioning temperature is too low.

english: The way to the beach is pretty.
grammar: 'caminho' — diminutive suffix expressing smallness, affection, or informality, not just physical size.

target: Eu trouxe o contrato para o escritório.

english: He fixed the phone in half an hour.

english: We looked for the restaurant for an hour.

target: Eu pus as compras na mesa da cozinha.
english: I put the groceries on the kitchen table.
grammar: Definite articles agree in gender and number: o/a/os/as. Portuguese uses articles more than English.

target: O hotel é simples, mas limpo e confortável.
english: The hotel is simple but clean and comfortable.
grammar: 'Com' contracts with pronouns: comigo (with me), contigo (with you), consigo (with himself/herself/yourself formal).

target: O bairro da Lapa é famoso pela vida noturna.

target: Minha mãe é a mulher mais forte que eu conheço.

target: Ele gastou muito dinheiro na reforma.
english: He spent a lot of money on the renovation.
grammar: Regular -ar past: gastar → gastou. 'Gastar' = to spend (money). 'Na reforma' = on the renovation.

target: Meu irmão mais novo é o mais alto da família.
english: My younger brother is the tallest in the family.
grammar: 'Mais novo' = younger, 'mais alto' = tallest/taller. 'O mais + adjective + da' = the most...of (superlative).

target: O sotaque dos gaúchos é diferente.

target: Eles são muito unidos.
english: They're very close-knit.
grammar: When a preposition meets an indefinite article, contraction is optional in some cases: 'dum/duma' exist but 'de um/de uma' is also fine.

grammar: 'Se fala' — impersonal construction with 'se', expressing a general statement about what 'one does' or 'is done'.

target: A gente gosta de fazer trilha.

target: Tchau, até mais!

english: Do you like barbecue?

target: A paisagem é deslumbrante.
english: The landscape is breathtaking.
grammar: Contractions with 'aqui/ali/aquilo': de+aqui=daqui (from here), de+ali=dali (from there) — common in everyday speech.

target: O jantar estava maravilhoso.
english: The dinner was wonderful.

english: Do you like sertanejo music?

target: Eu gosto muito de praia.
english: I really like the beach.
grammar: 'Gostar de' always requires the preposition 'de.' You can't say 'gosto praia' — it must be 'gosto de praia.'

target: As crianças estão agitadas hoje.
english: The kids are hyper today.
grammar: Contractions happen automatically in speech but must be written correctly: 'no parque' not 'em o parque'.

target: A comida está salgada demais.
english: The food is too salty.
grammar: Plural contractions follow the same pattern: de+os=dos, em+as=nas, a+os=aos — the rule applies to all number/gender combos.

target: Ainda bem que deu certo.
english: Thank goodness it worked out.
grammar: 'Ainda bem que' means 'thank goodness that' or 'it's a good thing that.' Expresses relief.

target: Ela gosta muito do trabalho dela.
english: She really likes her job.

target: Ela não gosta de gente mal-educada.
english: She doesn't like rude people.

target: A minha avó é muito carinhosa.
english: My grandmother is very affectionate.
grammar: 'Carinhosa' — feminine -osa ending to match 'avó' (grandmother). Masculine: 'carinhoso.'

target: Ela é loira de olhos azuis.
english: She's blonde with blue eyes.
grammar: 'De olhos azuis' is how you describe eye color in Portuguese — literally 'of blue eyes.' Same pattern for hair: de cabelos pretos.

target: Com licença, onde fica o banheiro?
english: Excuse me, where's the bathroom?
grammar: 'Com licença' is used when you need to get past someone or interrupt politely. It's more common than 'desculpe' for these situations.

target: Até amanhã, descansa!
english: See you tomorrow, get some rest!
grammar: The perfeito often pairs with time markers: 'ontem' (yesterday), 'na semana passada' (last week), 'em 2020'.

target: Boa viagem! Manda notícias.
english: Have a good trip! Send news.
grammar: Don't confuse perfeito with the present perfect — Portuguese 'tenho feito' implies ongoing/recent action, not a completed one.

target: Nós preferimos ir de carro.
english: We prefer to go by car.
grammar: 'Preferir' = to prefer. Unlike 'gostar' and 'precisar,' it does NOT take 'de': 'preferimos ir' (not 'de ir').

target: Eles preferem viajar de avião.
english: They prefer to travel by plane.

target: Que saco, perdi o ônibus!
english: How annoying, I missed the bus!
grammar: The perfeito tells the story — it moves the narrative forward with completed events, one after another.

english: Did you make a hotel reservation?

target: Pois não? Em que posso ajudar?
english: Yes? How can I help you?
grammar: 'Pois não' is a formal/polite way to say 'how can I help you.' You'll hear it from shopkeepers, receptionists, and servers.

target: Sabe de uma coisa? Eu desisto.
english: You know what? I give up.
grammar: The perfeito of 'ser' and 'ir' are identical: 'fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram' — context makes the meaning clear.

target: A gente gosta de viajar no Carnaval.
english: We like to travel during Carnival.
grammar: 'A gente gosta de' — remember 'a gente' takes singular: 'gosta' not 'gostamos.' 'No Carnaval' = during Carnival.

target: Ela gosta de ler antes de dormir.
english: She likes to read before bed.
grammar: 'Gostar de' + infinitive: 'gosta de ler.' 'Antes de' = before. 'Antes de dormir' = before sleeping.

target: Eu gosto de tomar banho de chuva.
english: I like showering in the rain.
grammar: Unlike Spanish 'gustar,' Portuguese 'gostar' works normally: 'eu gosto de música' (I like music) — subject is the person.

target: Eu gosto de ouvir música ao vivo.

target: Os filhos dela são educados e obedientes.
english: Her children are polite and obedient.
grammar: 'Educados e obedientes' — plural adjectives agree with plural noun 'filhos.' 'Dela' = de + ela = her.

target: A minha cachorra é pequena e branca.
english: My dog is small and white.
grammar: Colors agree with gender and number: branco/branca/brancos/brancas. Some colors don't change: laranja, rosa, violeta.

target: Obrigado pela ajuda, eu agradeço.
english: Thanks for the help, I appreciate it.
grammar: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Eu vi ela no supermercado ontem.
english: I saw her at the supermarket yesterday.
grammar: 'Ver' past: eu vi. 'Vi ela' is informal; formal would be 'a vi.' But 'vi ela' is standard in speech.

target: Ela quis saber todos os detalhes.
english: She wanted to know all the details.
grammar: Use imperfect for past states of mind and feelings: 'Ela queria ir' (She wanted to go), 'Eu sabia a resposta' (I knew the answer).

target: Ela tem cabelos longos e olhos escuros.
english: She has long hair and dark eyes.
grammar: Contractions extend to demonstratives: de+este=deste, em+aquele=naquele, a+aquela=àquela. These are mandatory in all registers.

english: This is the best pizza in the city.
grammar: Superlatives use 'o/a mais' + adjective or irregular forms: o melhor (the best), o pior (the worst), o maior (the biggest).

target: O pior dia da semana é segunda-feira.
english: The worst day of the week is Monday.
grammar: 'De + o/a/os/as' always contracts to 'do/da/dos/das' — these contractions are mandatory, never optional.

target: Ela gravou a reunião para ouvir depois.
english: She recorded the meeting to listen to later.
grammar: Regular -ar past: gravar → gravou. 'Gravar' = to record. 'Para ouvir depois' = to listen later.

target: Ela almoçou com as amigas no sábado.
english: She had lunch with her friends on Saturday.

target: As ruas são estreitas e cheias de gente.
english: The streets are narrow and full of people.
grammar: Adjectives ending in -o change to -as in feminine plural: estreito → estreitas. Adjectives ending in -e stay the same for both genders: grande → grandes.

target: A rua é escura e perigosa à noite.
english: The street is dark and dangerous at night.
grammar: 'Escura e perigosa' — both adjectives in feminine to match 'rua' (street). 'À noite' = at night.

target: As meninas são tão estudiosas quanto os meninos.
english: The girls are as studious as the boys.
grammar: 'Tão...quanto' = as...as (comparison of equality). 'Tão estudiosas quanto' = as studious as.

target: Eu troquei o pneu do carro na estrada.
english: I changed the car tire on the road.
grammar: Regular -er/-ir preterite: -i, -este, -eu/-iu, -emos/-imos, -eram/-iram. The 1st person -i and 3rd person -eu/-iu are most used.

target: Ele é sério no trabalho, mas brincalhão em casa.
english: He's serious at work but playful at home.
grammar: 'Em + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'no/na/nos/nas' — always use the contracted form.

target: Eu acordei cedo e fui correr.
english: I woke up early and went for a run.

target: Ela cuidou das crianças enquanto eu trabalhei.
english: She took care of the kids while I worked.
grammar: 'Ser' and 'ir' share the same preterite forms: fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram — only context tells them apart.

target: A escola era pequena, mas todo mundo se conhecia.
english: The school was small, but everyone knew each other.
grammar: 'Se' can also indicate reciprocal action: 'eles se encontram' can mean 'they meet each other'.

target: O melhor café da cidade é nessa rua.
english: The best café in the city is on this street.
grammar: 'De + o/a/os/as' always contracts to 'do/da/dos/das' — these contractions are mandatory, never optional.

target: O vento está forte demais para ir à praia.
english: The wind is too strong to go to the beach.
grammar: 'A + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'ao/à/aos/às'. The grave accent on 'à' marks the contraction a + a (crase).

target: A vista daqui é a mais bonita da cidade.
english: The view from here is the most beautiful in the city.
grammar: 'De + o/a/os/as' always contracts to 'do/da/dos/das' — these contractions are mandatory, never optional.

target: Bora!
english: Let's go!
grammar: 'Bora' is a contraction of 'vamos embora' (let's go). It's possibly the most-used casual word in Brazilian Portuguese.

target: Que legal!
english: How cool!
grammar: 'Que legal' is the most common exclamation of approval in Brazil. 'Legal' literally means 'legal' but is used like 'cool/nice/great.'

target: Que massa!
english: That's awesome!
grammar: Perfeito signals a change of state: 'Ele ficou triste' (He became sad) — the sadness started at that moment.

target: Que maravilha!
english: How wonderful!
grammar: Regular -ar verbs in perfeito: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The -ei and -ou endings are the most common.

target: Que horror!
english: How horrible!
grammar: Regular -ar verbs in perfeito: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The -ei and -ou endings are the most common.

target: Que fofo!
english: How cute!
grammar: The perfeito tells the story — it moves the narrative forward with completed events, one after another.

target: Que loucura!
english: How crazy!
grammar: Don't confuse perfeito with the present perfect — Portuguese 'tenho feito' implies ongoing/recent action, not a completed one.

target: Que delícia!
english: How delicious!
grammar: Regular -ar verbs in perfeito: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The -ei and -ou endings are the most common.

target: Deus me livre!
english: God forbid!
grammar: The perfeito of 'ser' and 'ir' are identical: 'fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram' — context makes the meaning clear.

target: Que absurdo isso!
english: That's outrageous!
grammar: The perfeito of 'ser' and 'ir' are identical: 'fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram' — context makes the meaning clear.

target: Tô morrendo de fome!
english: I'm starving!
grammar: 'Morrendo de' + noun is how Brazilians exaggerate: morrendo de fome (starving), morrendo de sono (dead tired), morrendo de rir (dying of laughter).

target: Sério mesmo?
english: Really? For real?
grammar: When narrating a sequence of past events, use perfeito for each action: 'Acordei, tomei café e saí' (I woke up, had coffee, and left).

target: Manda ver!
english: Go for it!
grammar: For repeated past actions with a set number, use perfeito: 'Li o livro três vezes' (I read the book three times).

target: Tem certeza?
english: Are you sure?
grammar: Regular -ar verbs in perfeito: -ei, -aste (BP: -ou), -ou, -ámos, -aram. The -ei and -ou endings are the most common.

target: Vamos nessa!
english: Let's do this!
grammar: Choose perfeito over imperfect when the action happened at a specific time: 'Ela chegou às três' (She arrived at three).

target: Que bagunça!
english: What a mess!
grammar: The perfeito often pairs with time markers: 'ontem' (yesterday), 'na semana passada' (last week), 'em 2020'.

target: Deixa eu ver...
english: Let me see...
grammar: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Cara, que difícil!
english: Man, that's tough!
grammar: Don't confuse perfeito with the present perfect — Portuguese 'tenho feito' implies ongoing/recent action, not a completed one.

target: Fica pra próxima.
english: Maybe next time.
grammar: 'Fica pra próxima' is the polite way to turn down an invitation while leaving the door open for future plans.

target: Ai meu Deus!
english: Oh my God!
grammar: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Que bacana, parabéns!
english: How nice, congratulations!
grammar: 'Bacana' means nice/cool/great. It's a bit more grown-up than 'legal' and less slangy than 'massa.'

target: Eu acho que sim.
english: I think so.
grammar: For repeated past actions with a set number, use perfeito: 'Li o livro três vezes' (I read the book three times).

target: Eu tô nem aí.
english: I don't care.
grammar: 'Tô nem aí' is a casual way to say 'I don't care.' Somewhat dismissive — use with friends, not your boss.

target: Eu tô morrendo de sono.
english: I'm dead tired.
grammar: 'morrendo' — gerund form for ongoing action. Brazilian Portuguese prefers 'estar + gerund' over European Portuguese's 'estar a + infinitive'.

target: Que susto você me deu!
english: You scared me!
grammar: Regular -er/-ir verbs: the eu form in the preterite ends in -i, the ele/ela form in -eu/-iu.

target: Não acredito!
english: I can't believe it!
grammar: For repeated past actions with a set number, use perfeito: 'Li o livro três vezes' (I read the book three times).

target: Tamo junto!
english: We're in this together!
grammar: 'Tamo junto' is a contraction of 'estamos juntos.' It's a way of showing solidarity and friendship in Brazil.
